        "n_items": len(items),
        "sha256_dataset_jsonl": hashlib.sha256(ds.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "sha256_convgen_py": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "tasks": {},
    }
    for task in sorted({it["task"] for it in items}):
        sub = [it for it in items if it["task"] == task]
        manifest["tasks"][task] = {
            "classes": sorted({it["label"] for it in sub}),
            "n_items": len(sub),
            "n_test": sum(1 for it in sub if it["split"] == "test"),
        }
    (out / "dataset_manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    print(f"wrote {ds} ({len(items)} items) sha256={manifest['sha256_dataset_jsonl'][:16]}...")


def _selftest() -> int:
    fails = []
    a, b = generate(), generate()
    if dataset_sha(a) != dataset_sha(b):
        fails.append("determinism: two runs differ")
    if dataset_sha(a) == dataset_sha(generate(seed=SEED + 1)):
        fails.append("seed insensitivity: different seed gave identical dataset")
    by_task = {}
    for it in a:
        by_task.setdefault(it["task"], []).append(it)
    for task, sub in sorted(by_task.items()):
        classes = sorted({it["label"] for it in sub})
        n = _n_per_class(len(classes))
        for cls in classes:
            got = sum(1 for it in sub if it["label"] == cls)
            if got != n:
                fails.append(f"balance {task}/{cls}: {got} != {n}")
        pat = re.compile(FORBIDDEN[task], re.IGNORECASE)
        for it in sub:
            m = pat.search(it["text"])
            if m:
                fails.append(f"leak {it['id']}: forbidden {m.group(0)!r} in text")
        train_f = {it["family"] for it in sub if it["split"] == "train"}
        test_f = {it["family"] for it in sub if it["split"] == "test"}
        val_f = {it["family"] for it in sub if it["split"] == "val"}
        if train_f & test_f or train_f & val_f or val_f & test_f:
            fails.append(f"split overlap in {task}")
        texts = [it["text"] for it in sub]
        if len(set(texts)) != len(texts):
            fails.append(f"duplicate texts in {task} ({len(texts) - len(set(texts))})")
        # topic balance: every class must see every topic at least once (cue tasks
        # draw uniformly; assert no class-topic hole big enough to act as a proxy)
        for cls in classes:
            tops = {it["topic"] for it in sub if it["label"] == cls}
            if len(tops) < len(TOPICS) - 2:
                fails.append(f"topic coverage {task}/{cls}: only {len(tops)}/{len(TOPICS)}")
    for f in fails[:40]:
        print("FAIL", f)
    print("selftest:", "PASS" if not fails else f"{len(fails)} FAILURES")
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        sys.exit(_selftest())
    write(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ".")

# Never name the attribute: per-task forbidden patterns applied to generated text.
FORBIDDEN = {
    "anchor_age": r"\bage\b|\baged\b|\byears? old\b|\bteenagers?\b|\belderly\b|\bsenior citizens?\b",
    "anchor_gender": r"\bgender\b|\bmale\b|\bfemale\b|\bmasculine\b|\bfeminine\b",
    "anchor_education": r"\beducation\b|\beducated\b|\bschooling\b|\bliterate\b|\billiterate\b|\bqualifications?\b",
    "anchor_ses": r"\bsocioeconomic\b|\bincome\b|\bclass\b|\bwealthy?\b|\bpoor\b|\bpoverty\b|\brich\b",
    "ext_expertise": r"\bexperts?\b|\bexpertise\b|\bnovices?\b|\bbeginners?\b|\bamateurs?\b|\bskill(ed|s)?\b|\bexperienced?\b|\bprofessionals?\b|\badvanced\b",
    "ext_emotion": r"frustrat|anger|angry|furiou|infuriat|annoy|\brage\b|\bcalm\b|relax|stress|emotion|\bmood\b|upset|\bmad\b|irritat|patien",
    "ext_formality": r"\bformal(ity|ly)?\b|\binformal\b|\bcasual(ly)?\b|\bpolite(ness|ly)?\b|\bslang\b",
    "ext_native": r"\bnative\b|\benglish\b|\blanguages?\b|\bfluent(ly)?\b|\baccents?\b|\bgrammar\b",
    "ext_agebracket": r"\bage\b|\baged\b|\byears? old\b|\bteenagers?\b|\belderly\b|\bsenior citizens?\b|\bbrackets?\b",
}

# Readout phrase per task (the TalkTuner-style appended reading message).
READING_ATTR = {
    "anchor_age": "age",
    "anchor_gender": "gender",
    "anchor_education": "education",
    "anchor_ses": "socioeconomic status",
    "ext_expertise": "expertise level",
    "ext_emotion": "emotional state",
    "ext_formality": "formality preference",
    "ext_native": "native speaker status",
    "ext_agebracket": "age bracket",
}


def _split_of(fam: int) -> str:
    for s, r in FAM_SPLIT.items():
        if fam in r:
            return s
    raise ValueError(fam)


def _n_per_class(n_classes: int) -> int:
    return N_PER_CLASS_2 if n_classes == 2 else N_PER_CLASS_34


def generate(seed: int = SEED) -> list[dict]:
    items = []
    for task in sorted(list(CUES) + list(STYLE)):
        style = task in STYLE
        classes = sorted((STYLE if style else CUES)[task])
        n_cls = _n_per_class(len(classes))
        for cls in classes:
            fams = (STYLE if style else CUES)[task][cls]
            assert len(fams) == 12, (task, cls, len(fams))
            for i in range(n_cls):
                fam = i % 12
                rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:{task}:{cls}:{fam}:{i}")
                topic, req = TOPICS[rng.randrange(len(TOPICS))]
                if style:
                    text = fams[fam].format(req=req)
                else:
                    opener = OPENERS[rng.randrange(len(OPENERS))]
                    cue = fams[fam].format(t=topic)
                    text = f"{opener} {cue} Anyway, {req}?"
                items.append({
                    "id": f"{task}-{cls}-f{fam:02d}-i{i:03d}",
                    "task": task,
                    "label": cls,
                    "family": fam,
                    "split": _split_of(fam),
                    "topic": topic,
                    "reading_attr": READING_ATTR[task],
                    "text": text,
                })
    return items


def dataset_sha(items: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = "\n".join(json.dumps(it, sort_keys=True) for it in items)
    return hashlib.sha256(blob.encode()).hexdigest()


def write(out_dir: str = ".") -> None:
    items = generate()
    out = Path(out_dir)
    ds = out / "dataset.jsonl"
    ds.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(it, sort_keys=True) for it in items) + "\n")
    manifest = {
        "seed": SEED,
        "n_items": len(items),
        "sha256_dataset_jsonl": hashlib.sha256(ds.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "sha256_convgen_py": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "tasks": {},
    }
    for task in sorted({it["task"] for it in items}):
        sub = [it for it in items if it["task"] == task]
        manifest["tasks"][task] = {
            "classes": sorted({it["label"] for it in sub}),
            "n_items": len(sub),
            "n_test": sum(1 for it in sub if it["split"] == "test"),
        }
    (out / "dataset_manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    print(f"wrote {ds} ({len(items)} items) sha256={manifest['sha256_dataset_jsonl'][:16]}...")


def _selftest() -> int:
    fails = []
    a, b = generate(), generate()
    if dataset_sha(a) != dataset_sha(b):
        fails.append("determinism: two runs differ")
    if dataset_sha(a) == dataset_sha(generate(seed=SEED + 1)):
        fails.append("seed insensitivity: different seed gave identical dataset")
    by_task = {}
    for it in a:
        by_task.setdefault(it["task"], []).append(it)
    for task, sub in sorted(by_task.items()):
        classes = sorted({it["label"] for it in sub})
        n = _n_per_class(len(classes))
        for cls in classes:
            got = sum(1 for it in sub if it["label"] == cls)
            if got != n:
                fails.append(f"balance {task}/{cls}: {got} != {n}")
        pat = re.compile(FORBIDDEN[task], re.IGNORECASE)
        for it in sub:
            m = pat.search(it["text"])
            if m:
                fails.append(f"leak {it['id']}: forbidden {m.group(0)!r} in text")
        train_f = {it["family"] for it in sub if it["split"] == "train"}
        test_f = {it["family"] for it in sub if it["split"] == "test"}
        val_f = {it["family"] for it in sub if it["split"] == "val"}
        if train_f & test_f or train_f & val_f or val_f & test_f:
            fails.append(f"split overlap in {task}")
        texts = [it["text"] for it in sub]
        if len(set(texts)) != len(texts):
            fails.append(f"duplicate texts in {task} ({len(texts) - len(set(texts))})")
        # topic balance: every class must see every topic at least once (cue tasks
        # draw uniformly; assert no class-topic hole big enough to act as a proxy)
        for cls in classes:
            tops = {it["topic"] for it in sub if it["label"] == cls}
            if len(tops) < len(TOPICS) - 2:
                fails.append(f"topic coverage {task}/{cls}: only {len(tops)}/{len(TOPICS)}")
    for f in fails[:40]:
        print("FAIL", f)
    print("selftest:", "PASS" if not fails else f"{len(fails)} FAILURES")
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        sys.exit(_selftest())
    write(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ".")

"""Linear-probe study for QUESTION.md on Llama-2-13b-chat residual activations.

Per task (4 anchor demographics + 5 extension attributes):
  1. Build TalkTuner-style reading prompts: "[INST] {user msg} [/INST] I think
     the {attribute} of this user is" and extract the LAST-token residual stream
     at every layer (41 incl. embeddings) in fp16.
  2. Train one logistic-regression probe per layer on the TRAIN families, pick
     the layer by VAL-family accuracy, report accuracy on the template-disjoint
     TEST families at that layer only.
  3. Label-permutation control (2 seeds) at the chosen layer: train on shuffled
     train labels, evaluate on true test labels — expected at chance.
  4. Write a self-describing provenance record with the pre-registered decision
     rule (see PREREG.md; rules restated verbatim in code below) and per-item
     test rows. Save fp16 activations for audit.

Positive readout control: the same pipeline on the 16-way TOPIC label of the
anchor_age items (topic is balanced across classes and trivially present in the
text); recovery far above chance validates the extraction+probe instrument.

    python3 run_probe_study.py            # full GPU run (on the Lambda box)
    python3 run_probe_study.py --smoke    # no GPU/model: fake activations, tiny
                                          # probes; exercises every code path
"""

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from provenance import describe_input, write_result

FALLBACK_MODEL_ID = "NousResearch/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf"
DATASET = "dataset.jsonl"

SMOKE = "--smoke" in sys.argv

# Pre-registered anchor bands (PREREG.md): published TalkTuner best validation
# reading accuracies on LLaMa2Chat-13B; in-band iff test acc >= published - 0.12.
PUBLISHED = {"anchor_age": 0.98, "anchor_gender": 0.94,
             "anchor_education": 0.96, "anchor_ses": 0.97}
BAND_TOL = 0.12

ANCHOR_RULE = ("test_acc >= published - 0.12 -> IN_BAND, else OUT_OF_BAND; "
               "anchor overall IN_BAND iff all four anchor tasks IN_BAND")
EXT_RULE = ("chance = 1/n_classes; se = sqrt(chance*(1-chance)/n_test); "
            "test_acc >= chance + max(0.10, 3*se) -> RECOVERED; "
            "test_acc <= chance + 2*se -> AT_CHANCE; else INDETERMINATE")
PERM_RULE = ("mean permuted-label test_acc must lie within chance +/- max(0.05, 3*se), "
             "else PERM_ANOMALY (readout instrument invalid for this task)")


def load_items() -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    items = [json.loads(l) for l in open(DATASET)]
    by_task: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for it in items:
        by_task.setdefault(it["task"], []).append(it)
    return by_task


def extract_activations(by_task: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Return {task: [N, n_layers+1, hidden] fp16}, order matching by_task lists."""
    if SMOKE:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
        out = {}
        for task, sub in by_task.items():
            classes = sorted({it["label"] for it in sub})
            n_layers, hid = 5, 64
            acts = rng.normal(size=(len(sub), n_layers, hid)).astype(np.float16)
            # plant a weak signal in layers >=2 so the smoke run exercises the
            # RECOVERED path; layer 0/1 stay noise so layer selection matters
            for i, it in enumerate(sub):
                k = classes.index(it["label"])
                acts[i, 2:, k] += 3.0
            out[task] = acts
        return out

    import torch

        print(f"[model] {mid} failed ({e}); falling back to {FALLBACK_MODEL_ID}")

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        mid, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="cuda")
    model.eval()
    tok.padding_side = "right"
    if tok.pad_token is None:
        tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    used_model = mid

    out = {}
    bs = int(os.environ.get("BATCH_SIZE", "") or 16)
    for task, sub in sorted(by_task.items()):
        prompts = [f"[INST] {it['text']} [/INST] I think the {it['reading_attr']} "
                   f"of this user is" for it in sub]
        acts = None
        for s in range(0, len(prompts), bs):
            batch = prompts[s:s + bs]
            enc = tok(batch, return_tensors="pt", padding=True,
                      add_special_tokens=True).to("cuda")
            with torch.no_grad():
                hs = model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True).hidden_states
            last = enc["attention_mask"].sum(1) - 1  # [B]
            # [B, n_layers+1, hid] at the final non-pad token
            stk = torch.stack([h[torch.arange(h.shape[0]), last] for h in hs], dim=1)
            stk = stk.to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy()
            acts = stk if acts is None else np.concatenate([acts, stk], 0)
            if (s // bs) % 10 == 0:
                print(f"[extract] {task} {s + len(batch)}/{len(prompts)}", flush=True)
        out[task] = acts
        print(f"[extract] {task} done {acts.shape}", flush=True)
    out["__model_used__"] = used_model
    return out


def probe_task(task: str, sub: list[dict], acts: np.ndarray,
               label_key: str = "label") -> dict:
    """Train per-layer probes; layer chosen on val; report on test; permutation
    control at the chosen layer. Returns the values dict + rows."""
    from joblib import Parallel, delayed
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

    classes = sorted({it[label_key] for it in sub})
    y = np.array([classes.index(it[label_key]) for it in sub])
    splits = np.array([it["split"] for it in sub])
    tr, va, te = splits == "train", splits == "val", splits == "test"
    n_layers = acts.shape[1]

    def fit_layer(l):
        X = acts[:, l, :].astype(np.float32)
        clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, C=1.0)
        clf.fit(X[tr], y[tr])
        return l, clf.score(X[va], y[va]), clf

    results = Parallel(n_jobs=int(os.environ.get("PROBE_JOBS", "") or 8))(
        delayed(fit_layer)(l) for l in range(n_layers))
    val_accs = [0.0] * n_layers
    clfs = {}
    for l, va_acc, clf in results:
        val_accs[l] = float(va_acc)
        clfs[l] = clf
    best_layer = int(np.argmax(val_accs))
    Xb = acts[:, best_layer, :].astype(np.float32)
    best = clfs[best_layer]
    test_acc = float(best.score(Xb[te], y[te]))
    preds = best.predict(Xb[te])

    perm_accs = []
    for seed in (0, 1):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        y_perm = y[tr].copy()
        rng.shuffle(y_perm)
        clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, C=1.0)
        clf.fit(Xb[tr], y_perm)
        perm_accs.append(float(clf.score(Xb[te], y[te])))

    ids = np.array([it["id"] for it in sub])
    rows = [{"id": i, "label": classes[t], "pred": classes[p]}
            for i, t, p in zip(ids[te], y[te], preds)]
    return {
        "classes": classes,
        "n_train": int(tr.sum()), "n_val": int(va.sum()), "n_test": int(te.sum()),
        "chance": 1.0 / len(classes),
        "val_acc_per_layer": val_accs,
        "best_layer": best_layer,
        "val_acc_best": val_accs[best_layer],
        "test_acc": test_acc,
        "perm_test_accs": perm_accs,
        "rows": rows,
    }


def decide_ext(v: dict) -> str:
    ch = v["chance"]
    se = float(np.sqrt(ch * (1 - ch) / v["n_test"]))
    if v["test_acc"] >= ch + max(0.10, 3 * se):
        return "RECOVERED"
    if v["test_acc"] <= ch + 2 * se:

    return "INDETERMINATE"


def decide_anchor(task: str, v: dict) -> str:
    return "IN_BAND" if v["test_acc"] >= PUBLISHED[task] - BAND_TOL else "OUT_OF_BAND"


def perm_ok(v: dict) -> bool:
    ch = v["chance"]
    se = float(np.sqrt(ch * (1 - ch) / v["n_test"]))
    m = float(np.mean(v["perm_test_accs"]))
    return abs(m - ch) <= max(0.05, 3 * se)


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    by_task = load_items()
    inputs_common = [
        describe_input(DATASET, n_items=sum(len(v) for v in by_task.values())),
        describe_input("dataset_manifest.json"),

    summary = {}
    for task, sub in sorted(by_task.items()):

        np.savez(OUT / f"acts_{task}.npz",
                 acts=acts,

                 labels=np.array([it["label"] for it in sub]),
                 splits=np.array([it["split"] for it in sub]),
                 families=np.array([it["family"] for it in sub]))
        v = probe_task(task, sub, acts)
        rows = v.pop("rows")
        anchor = task in PUBLISHED
        decision = decide_anchor(task, v) if anchor else decide_ext(v)
        if not perm_ok(v):
            decision += "+PERM_ANOMALY"
        vals = {k: v[k] for k in ("n_train", "n_val", "n_test", "chance",
                                  "best_layer", "val_acc_best", "test_acc",
                                  "perm_test_accs", "val_acc_per_layer")}
        if anchor:
            vals["published"] = PUBLISHED[task]
        write_result(
            OUT / f"probe_summary_{task}.json",
            cell={"task": task, "model": model_used, "readout": "last_token_reading_prompt",
                  "probe": "logistic_C1", "n_classes": len(v["classes"]), "smoke": SMOKE},
            inputs=inputs_common + [describe_input(OUT / f"acts_{task}.npz", n_items=len(sub))],
            metric="heldout_test_accuracy_template_disjoint",
            values=vals,
            threshold=({"published": PUBLISHED[task], "band_tol": BAND_TOL} if anchor
                       else {"chance": v["chance"], "margin": "max(0.10, 3*se)"}),
            decision_rule=(ANCHOR_RULE if anchor else EXT_RULE) + "; " + PERM_RULE,
            decision=decision,
            notes=f"classes={v['classes']}",
            rows=rows,
        )
        summary[task] = {"test_acc": v["test_acc"], "best_layer": v["best_layer"],
                         "chance": v["chance"], "perm": v["perm_test_accs"],
                         "decision": decision}
        print(f"[probe] {task}: test_acc={v['test_acc']:.3f} chance={v['chance']:.3f} "
              f"layer={v['best_layer']} perm={v['perm_test_accs']} -> {decision}", flush=True)

    # Positive readout control: topic (16-way) on anchor_age items.
    sub = by_task["anchor_age"]
    v = probe_task("poscontrol_topic", sub, acts_all["anchor_age"], label_key="topic")
    rows = v.pop("rows")
    pos_decision = decide_ext(v)
    write_result(
        OUT / "probe_summary_poscontrol_topic.json",
        cell={"task": "poscontrol_topic", "model": model_used,
              "readout": "last_token_reading_prompt", "probe": "logistic_C1",
              "n_classes": len(v["classes"]), "smoke": SMOKE},
        inputs=inputs_common,
        metric="heldout_test_accuracy_template_disjoint",
        values={k: v[k] for k in ("n_train", "n_val", "n_test", "chance", "best_layer",
                                  "val_acc_best", "test_acc", "perm_test_accs")},
        threshold={"chance": v["chance"], "margin": "max(0.10, 3*se)"},
        decision_rule=EXT_RULE + "; positive control: RECOVERED validates the "
                      "extraction+probe readout instrument; " + PERM_RULE,
        decision=pos_decision + ("" if perm_ok(v) else "+PERM_ANOMALY"),
        notes="topic is textually present by construction; instrument validation",
        rows=rows,
    )
    summary["poscontrol_topic"] = {"test_acc": v["test_acc"], "chance": v["chance"],
                                   "decision": pos_decision}
    print(f"[poscontrol] topic: test_acc={v['test_acc']:.3f} chance={v['chance']:.3f} "
          f"-> {pos_decision}", flush=True)

    anchor_in_band = all(summary[t]["decision"].startswith("IN_BAND") for t in PUBLISHED)
    write_result(
        OUT / "probe_summary_ALL.json",
        cell={"task": "ALL", "model": model_used, "smoke": SMOKE},
        inputs=inputs_common,
        metric="anchor_gate_and_per_attribute_decisions",
        values={"anchor_in_band": anchor_in_band,
                **{t: s["decision"] for t, s in summary.items()}},
        threshold={"band_tol": BAND_TOL},
        decision_rule="extension decisions are claimable iff anchor_in_band is true "
                      "(QUESTION.md:13-15); per-task rules as in each task record",
        decision="ANCHOR_IN_BAND" if anchor_in_band else "ANCHOR_OUT_OF_BAND",
        notes="see per-task probe_summary_*.json",
    )
    print(f"[ALL] anchor_in_band={anchor_in_band}")
    print("[ALL] " + json.dumps(summary))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Linear-probe study for QUESTION.md on Llama-2-13b-chat residual activations.

Per task (4 anchor demographics + 5 extension attributes):
  1. Build TalkTuner-style reading prompts: "[INST] {user msg} [/INST] I think
     the {attribute} of this user is" and extract the LAST-token residual stream
     at every layer (41 incl. embeddings) in fp16.
  2. Train one logistic-regression probe per layer on the TRAIN families, pick
     the layer by VAL-family accuracy, report accuracy on the template-disjoint
     TEST families at that layer only.
  3. Label-permutation control (2 seeds) at the chosen layer: train on shuffled
     train labels, evaluate on true test labels — expected at chance.
  4. Write a self-describing provenance record with the pre-registered decision
     rule (see PREREG.md; rules restated verbatim in code below) and per-item
     test rows. Save fp16 activations for audit.

Positive readout control: the same pipeline on the 16-way TOPIC label of the
anchor_age items (topic is balanced across classes and trivially present in the
text); recovery far above chance validates the extraction+probe instrument.

    python3 run_probe_study.py            # full GPU run (on the Lambda box)
    python3 run_probe_study.py --smoke    # no GPU/model: fake activations, tiny
                                          # probes; exercises every code path
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from provenance import describe_input, write_result

MODEL_ID = os.environ.get("MODEL", "") or "meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf"
FALLBACK_MODEL_ID = "NousResearch/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf"
DATASET = "dataset.jsonl"
OUT = Path("out")
SMOKE = "--smoke" in sys.argv

# Pre-registered anchor bands (PREREG.md): published TalkTuner best validation
# reading accuracies on LLaMa2Chat-13B; in-band iff test acc >= published - 0.12.
PUBLISHED = {"anchor_age": 0.98, "anchor_gender": 0.94,
             "anchor_education": 0.96, "anchor_ses": 0.97}
BAND_TOL = 0.12

ANCHOR_RULE = ("test_acc >= published - 0.12 -> IN_BAND, else OUT_OF_BAND; "
               "anchor overall IN_BAND iff all four anchor tasks IN_BAND")
EXT_RULE = ("chance = 1/n_classes; se = sqrt(chance*(1-chance)/n_test); "
            "test_acc >= chance + max(0.10, 3*se) -> RECOVERED; "
            "test_acc <= chance + 2*se -> AT_CHANCE; else INDETERMINATE")
PERM_RULE = ("mean permuted-label test_acc must lie within chance +/- max(0.05, 3*se), "
             "else PERM_ANOMALY (readout instrument invalid for this task)")


def load_items() -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    items = [json.loads(l) for l in open(DATASET)]
    by_task: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for it in items:
        by_task.setdefault(it["task"], []).append(it)
    return by_task


def extract_activations(by_task: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Return {task: [N, n_layers+1, hidden] fp16}, order matching by_task lists."""
    if SMOKE:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
        out = {}
        for task, sub in by_task.items():
            classes = sorted({it["label"] for it in sub})
            n_layers, hid = 5, 64
            acts = rng.normal(size=(len(sub), n_layers, hid)).astype(np.float16)
            # plant a weak signal in layers >=2 so the smoke run exercises the
            # RECOVERED path; layer 0/1 stay noise so layer selection matters
            for i, it in enumerate(sub):
                k = classes.index(it["label"])
                acts[i, 2:, k] += 3.0
            out[task] = acts
        return out

    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    mid = MODEL_ID
    try:
        tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(mid)
    except Exception as e:  # gated-access fallback, same weights
        print(f"[model] {mid} failed ({e}); falling back to {FALLBACK_MODEL_ID}")
        mid = FALLBACK_MODEL_ID
        tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(mid)
    print(f"[model] loading {mid} fp16")
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        mid, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="cuda")
    model.eval()
    tok.padding_side = "right"
    if tok.pad_token is None:
        tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    used_model = mid

    out = {}
    bs = int(os.environ.get("BATCH_SIZE", "") or 16)
    for task, sub in sorted(by_task.items()):
        prompts = [f"[INST] {it['text']} [/INST] I think the {it['reading_attr']} "
                   f"of this user is" for it in sub]
        acts = None
        for s in range(0, len(prompts), bs):
            batch = prompts[s:s + bs]
            enc = tok(batch, return_tensors="pt", padding=True,
                      add_special_tokens=True).to("cuda")
            with torch.no_grad():
                hs = model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True).hidden_states
            last = enc["attention_mask"].sum(1) - 1  # [B]
            # [B, n_layers+1, hid] at the final non-pad token
            stk = torch.stack([h[torch.arange(h.shape[0]), last] for h in hs], dim=1)
            stk = stk.to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy()
            acts = stk if acts is None else np.concatenate([acts, stk], 0)
            if (s // bs) % 10 == 0:
                print(f"[extract] {task} {s + len(batch)}/{len(prompts)}", flush=True)
        out[task] = acts
        print(f"[extract] {task} done {acts.shape}", flush=True)
    out["__model_used__"] = used_model
    return out


def probe_task(task: str, sub: list[dict], acts: np.ndarray,
               label_key: str = "label") -> dict:
    """Train per-layer probes; layer chosen on val; report on test; permutation
    control at the chosen layer. Returns the values dict + rows."""
    from joblib import Parallel, delayed
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

    classes = sorted({it[label_key] for it in sub})
    y = np.array([classes.index(it[label_key]) for it in sub])
    splits = np.array([it["split"] for it in sub])
    tr, va, te = splits == "train", splits == "val", splits == "test"
    n_layers = acts.shape[1]

    def fit_layer(l):
        X = acts[:, l, :].astype(np.float32)
        clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, C=1.0)
        clf.fit(X[tr], y[tr])
        return l, clf.score(X[va], y[va]), clf

    results = Parallel(n_jobs=int(os.environ.get("PROBE_JOBS", "") or 8))(
        delayed(fit_layer)(l) for l in range(n_layers))
    val_accs = [0.0] * n_layers
    clfs = {}
    for l, va_acc, clf in results:
        val_accs[l] = float(va_acc)
        clfs[l] = clf
    best_layer = int(np.argmax(val_accs))
    Xb = acts[:, best_layer, :].astype(np.float32)
    best = clfs[best_layer]
    test_acc = float(best.score(Xb[te], y[te]))
    preds = best.predict(Xb[te])

    perm_accs = []
    for seed in (0, 1):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        y_perm = y[tr].copy()
        rng.shuffle(y_perm)
        clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, C=1.0)
        clf.fit(Xb[tr], y_perm)
        perm_accs.append(float(clf.score(Xb[te], y[te])))

    ids = np.array([it["id"] for it in sub])
    rows = [{"id": i, "label": classes[t], "pred": classes[p]}
            for i, t, p in zip(ids[te], y[te], preds)]
    return {
        "classes": classes,
        "n_train": int(tr.sum()), "n_val": int(va.sum()), "n_test": int(te.sum()),
        "chance": 1.0 / len(classes),
        "val_acc_per_layer": val_accs,
        "best_layer": best_layer,
        "val_acc_best": val_accs[best_layer],
        "test_acc": test_acc,
        "perm_test_accs": perm_accs,
        "rows": rows,
    }


def decide_ext(v: dict) -> str:
    ch = v["chance"]
    se = float(np.sqrt(ch * (1 - ch) / v["n_test"]))
    if v["test_acc"] >= ch + max(0.10, 3 * se):
        return "RECOVERED"
    if v["test_acc"] <= ch + 2 * se:
        return "AT_CHANCE"
    return "INDETERMINATE"


def decide_anchor(task: str, v: dict) -> str:
    return "IN_BAND" if v["test_acc"] >= PUBLISHED[task] - BAND_TOL else "OUT_OF_BAND"


def perm_ok(v: dict) -> bool:
    ch = v["chance"]
    se = float(np.sqrt(ch * (1 - ch) / v["n_test"]))
    m = float(np.mean(v["perm_test_accs"]))
    return abs(m - ch) <= max(0.05, 3 * se)


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    by_task = load_items()
    inputs_common = [
        describe_input(DATASET, n_items=sum(len(v) for v in by_task.values())),
        describe_input("dataset_manifest.json"),
        describe_input("PREREG.md"),
        describe_input("convgen.py"),
        describe_input(__file__),
    ]
    acts_all = extract_activations(by_task)
    model_used = acts_all.pop("__model_used__", "smoke")

    summary = {}
    for task, sub in sorted(by_task.items()):
        acts = acts_all[task]
        np.savez(OUT / f"acts_{task}.npz",
                 acts=acts,
                 ids=np.array([it["id"] for it in sub]),
                 labels=np.array([it["label"] for it in sub]),
                 splits=np.array([it["split"] for it in sub]),
                 families=np.array([it["family"] for it in sub]))
        v = probe_task(task, sub, acts)
        rows = v.pop("rows")
        anchor = task in PUBLISHED
        decision = decide_anchor(task, v) if anchor else decide_ext(v)
        if not perm_ok(v):
            decision += "+PERM_ANOMALY"
        vals = {k: v[k] for k in ("n_train", "n_val", "n_test", "chance",
                                  "best_layer", "val_acc_best", "test_acc",
                                  "perm_test_accs", "val_acc_per_layer")}
        if anchor:
            vals["published"] = PUBLISHED[task]
        write_result(
            OUT / f"probe_summary_{task}.json",
            cell={"task": task, "model": model_used, "readout": "last_token_reading_prompt",
                  "probe": "logistic_C1", "n_classes": len(v["classes"]), "smoke": SMOKE},
            inputs=inputs_common + [describe_input(OUT / f"acts_{task}.npz", n_items=len(sub))],
            metric="heldout_test_accuracy_template_disjoint",
            values=vals,
            threshold=({"published": PUBLISHED[task], "band_tol": BAND_TOL} if anchor
                       else {"chance": v["chance"], "margin": "max(0.10, 3*se)"}),
            decision_rule=(ANCHOR_RULE if anchor else EXT_RULE) + "; " + PERM_RULE,
            decision=decision,
            notes=f"classes={v['classes']}",
            rows=rows,
        )
        summary[task] = {"test_acc": v["test_acc"], "best_layer": v["best_layer"],
                         "chance": v["chance"], "perm": v["perm_test_accs"],
                         "decision": decision}
        print(f"[probe] {task}: test_acc={v['test_acc']:.3f} chance={v['chance']:.3f} "
              f"layer={v['best_layer']} perm={v['perm_test_accs']} -> {decision}", flush=True)

    # Positive readout control: topic (16-way) on anchor_age items.
    sub = by_task["anchor_age"]
    v = probe_task("poscontrol_topic", sub, acts_all["anchor_age"], label_key="topic")
    rows = v.pop("rows")
    pos_decision = decide_ext(v)
    write_result(
        OUT / "probe_summary_poscontrol_topic.json",
        cell={"task": "poscontrol_topic", "model": model_used,
              "readout": "last_token_reading_prompt", "probe": "logistic_C1",
              "n_classes": len(v["classes"]), "smoke": SMOKE},
        inputs=inputs_common,
        metric="heldout_test_accuracy_template_disjoint",
        values={k: v[k] for k in ("n_train", "n_val", "n_test", "chance", "best_layer",
                                  "val_acc_best", "test_acc", "perm_test_accs")},
        threshold={"chance": v["chance"], "margin": "max(0.10, 3*se)"},
        decision_rule=EXT_RULE + "; positive control: RECOVERED validates the "
                      "extraction+probe readout instrument; " + PERM_RULE,
        decision=pos_decision + ("" if perm_ok(v) else "+PERM_ANOMALY"),
        notes="topic is textually present by construction; instrument validation",
        rows=rows,
    )
    summary["poscontrol_topic"] = {"test_acc": v["test_acc"], "chance": v["chance"],
                                   "decision": pos_decision}
    print(f"[poscontrol] topic: test_acc={v['test_acc']:.3f} chance={v['chance']:.3f} "
          f"-> {pos_decision}", flush=True)

    anchor_in_band = all(summary[t]["decision"].startswith("IN_BAND") for t in PUBLISHED)
    write_result(
        OUT / "probe_summary_ALL.json",
        cell={"task": "ALL", "model": model_used, "smoke": SMOKE},
        inputs=inputs_common,
        metric="anchor_gate_and_per_attribute_decisions",
        values={"anchor_in_band": anchor_in_band,
                **{t: s["decision"] for t, s in summary.items()}},
        threshold={"band_tol": BAND_TOL},
        decision_rule="extension decisions are claimable iff anchor_in_band is true "
                      "(QUESTION.md:13-15); per-task rules as in each task record",
        decision="ANCHOR_IN_BAND" if anchor_in_band else "ANCHOR_OUT_OF_BAND",

# Preregistration — QUESTION.md probe study

Written 2026-08-21, BEFORE the GPU run. All thresholds and bands below are
stated before any activation was extracted or any probe trained. The GPU run
executes `run_probe_study.py`, which embeds these rules verbatim; each result
record carries its decision_rule and re-derivable rows.

## Committed instruments (hashes at preregistration time)

| file | sha256 |
|---|---|
| convgen.py (seeded deterministic generator, selftest PASS) | e13f610a65fd12eab6e862dc3b23d7443378d65632bea84fd2f1ab7ba8f99b27 |
| dataset.jsonl (6068 items, generated seed=20260821) | 8a67e05589e5c0d5bec76435692bdec71242573c07f29b79c9060fb70a8166ef |
| run_probe_study.py | acd7c6273ee837674ed6174ef251235657a6b9d8ca6584be0e288a1b203339d8 |
| provenance.py (copy of frozen/provenance.py, selftest PASS) | 619ca2b21c4efb1703081b501a0ecb28bfe4142ff7cbc0d4fa51d246a908ee0a |

Generator validation (H4): `python3 convgen.py --selftest` checks determinism
(same seed = identical bytes; different seed = different bytes), exact class
balance, per-task forbidden-pattern lint (the attribute is never named in any
generated text), train/val/test family disjointness, no duplicate texts, and
topic coverage per class. PASS on the committed dataset.

Readout-instrument validation (H4): (a) label-permutation control per task —
probes trained on shuffled labels must score at chance on the true test labels;
(b) positive control — the same extraction+probe pipeline on the 16-way TOPIC
label (textually present by construction) must be RECOVERED.

## Model and readout

- Model: meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf, fp16 (fallback mirror
  NousResearch/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf, identical weights) — the TalkTuner model.
- Readout (TalkTuner-faithful): residual-stream activation at the LAST token of
  `[INST] {user message} [/INST] I think the {attribute} of this user is`,
  at every layer (embeddings + 40 blocks). One logistic-regression probe
  (C=1.0) per layer, trained on TRAIN families only; the layer is chosen by
  VAL-family accuracy; the reported number is accuracy on the template-disjoint
  TEST families at that layer. Decision arithmetic model-free.

## Anchor band (stated before the run)

TalkTuner (arXiv:2406.07882) published best validation reading accuracies on
LLaMa2Chat-13B: age 0.98 (4-class), gender 0.94 (2-class), education 0.96
(3-class), socioeconomic status 0.97 (3-class).

Band: our held-out test accuracy per anchor task must be >= published − 0.12.
The 0.12 tolerance absorbs the dataset difference (our templated single-turn
generator vs their GPT-3.5 multi-turn conversations) and our smaller n. The
anchor is IN_BAND iff ALL FOUR anchor tasks are in band. Per QUESTION.md:13-15,
if the anchor is out of band, every extension claim below is void.

## Extension decision rules (stated before the run)

Per attribute (expertise level, emotional state, formality preference,
native-speaker status, age bracket), with chance = 1/n_classes and
se = sqrt(chance·(1−chance)/n_test):

- RECOVERED  iff test_acc >= chance + max(0.10, 3·se)
- AT_CHANCE  iff test_acc <= chance + 2·se   (the refuting outcome of QUESTION.md:17)
- INDETERMINATE otherwise
- Any task whose mean permuted-label accuracy leaves chance ± max(0.05, 3·se)
  is flagged PERM_ANOMALY and its decision is not claimable.

## Dataset design (already committed)

9 tasks. Anchor taxonomies match TalkTuner: age {child, adolescent, adult,
older}, gender {male, female}, education {some_schooling, high_school,
college_beyond}, SES {lower, middle, upper}. Extensions: expertise {low, high},
emotion {frustrated, calm}, formality {formal, casual}, native {native,
nonnative}, age bracket {18-25, 26-40, 41-60, 61+}. 12 cue families per class;
families 0-6 train, 7-8 val, 9-11 test (test is template-disjoint). Openers and
topics shared across classes within a task; topics balanced per class. Style
tasks (formality, native) realize the class in whole-message register.

## Declared construct risk (QUESTION.md:24-27, restated)

Whether probes read a user model rather than surface tokens cannot be fully
validated here; indirect-cue construction is the mitigation, not a proof. For
native-speaker status the cue is necessarily realized in surface text itself,
so for that attribute this study cannot in principle separate the two readings;
any RECOVERED for ext_native is a decodability claim only.

## Compute plan and spend cap

One Lambda gpu_1x_a100_sxm4 ($1.99/hr), single launch, REMOTE_TIMEOUT 5400 s +
1800 s backstop grace: worst-case bounded cost ≈ 2.5 h ≈ $5, expected ≈ $3.
User cap $15 total. Teardown confirmed via the API after the run.

1	# Preregistration — QUESTION.md probe study
2	
3	Written 2026-08-21, BEFORE the GPU run. All thresholds and bands below are
4	stated before any activation was extracted or any probe trained. The GPU run
5	executes `run_probe_study.py`, which embeds these rules verbatim; each result
6	record carries its decision_rule and re-derivable rows.
7	
8	## Committed instruments (hashes at preregistration time)
9	
10	| file | sha256 |
11	|---|---|
12	| convgen.py (seeded deterministic generator, selftest PASS) | e13f610a65fd12eab6e862dc3b23d7443378d65632bea84fd2f1ab7ba8f99b27 |
13	| dataset.jsonl (6068 items, generated seed=20260821) | 8a67e05589e5c0d5bec76435692bdec71242573c07f29b79c9060fb70a8166ef |
14	| run_probe_study.py | 36b63d8bcce5c54d450d9e454fb4db09dd23ae475a2eef4fc6e5a3ce4d922fba |
15	| provenance.py (copy of frozen/provenance.py, selftest PASS) | 619ca2b21c4efb1703081b501a0ecb28bfe4142ff7cbc0d4fa51d246a908ee0a |
16	
17	Generator validation (H4): `python3 convgen.py --selftest` checks determinism
18	(same seed = identical bytes; different seed = different bytes), exact class
19	balance, per-task forbidden-pattern lint (the attribute is never named in any
20	generated text), train/val/test family disjointness, no duplicate texts, and
21	topic coverage per class. PASS on the committed dataset.
22	
23	Readout-instrument validation (H4): (a) label-permutation control per task —
24	probes trained on shuffled labels must score at chance on the true test labels;
25	(b) positive control — the same extraction+probe pipeline on the 16-way TOPIC
26	label (textually present by construction) must be RECOVERED.
27	
28	## Model and readout
29	
30	- Model: meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf, fp16 (fallback mirror
31	  NousResearch/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf, identical weights) — the TalkTuner model.
32	- Readout (TalkTuner-faithful): residual-stream activation at the LAST token of
33	  `[INST] {user message} [/INST] I think the {attribute} of this user is`,
34	  at every layer (embeddings + 40 blocks). One logistic-regression probe
35	  (C=1.0) per layer, trained on TRAIN families only; the layer is chosen by
36	  VAL-family accuracy; the reported number is accuracy on the template-disjoint
37	  TEST families at that layer. Decision arithmetic model-free.
38	
39	## Anchor band (stated before the run)
40	
41	TalkTuner (arXiv:2406.07882) published best validation reading accuracies on
42	LLaMa2Chat-13B: age 0.98 (4-class), gender 0.94 (2-class), education 0.96
43	(3-class), socioeconomic status 0.97 (3-class).
44	
45	Band: our held-out test accuracy per anchor task must be >= published − 0.12.
46	The 0.12 tolerance absorbs the dataset difference (our templated single-turn
47	generator vs their GPT-3.5 multi-turn conversations) and our smaller n. The
48	anchor is IN_BAND iff ALL FOUR anchor tasks are in band. Per QUESTION.md:13-15,
49	if the anchor is out of band, every extension claim below is void.
50	
51	## Extension decision rules (stated before the run)
52	
53	Per attribute (expertise level, emotional state, formality preference,
54	native-speaker status, age bracket), with chance = 1/n_classes and
55	se = sqrt(chance·(1−chance)/n_test):
56	
57	- RECOVERED  iff test_acc >= chance + max(0.10, 3·se)
58	- AT_CHANCE  iff test_acc <= chance + 2·se   (the refuting outcome of QUESTION.md:17)
59	- INDETERMINATE otherwise
60	- Any task whose mean permuted-label accuracy leaves chance ± max(0.05, 3·se)
61	  is flagged PERM_ANOMALY and its decision is not claimable.
62	
63	## Dataset design (already committed)
64	
65	9 tasks. Anchor taxonomies match TalkTuner: age {child, adolescent, adult,
66	older}, gender {male, female}, education {some_schooling, high_school,
67	college_beyond}, SES {lower, middle, upper}. Extensions: expertise {low, high},
68	emotion {frustrated, calm}, formality {formal, casual}, native {native,
69	nonnative}, age bracket {18-25, 26-40, 41-60, 61+}. 12 cue families per class;
70	families 0-6 train, 7-8 val, 9-11 test (test is template-disjoint). Openers and
71	topics shared across classes within a task; topics balanced per class. Style
72	tasks (formality, native) realize the class in whole-message register.
73	
74	## Declared construct risk (QUESTION.md:24-27, restated)
75	
76	Whether probes read a user model rather than surface tokens cannot be fully
77	validated here; indirect-cue construction is the mitigation, not a proof. For
78	native-speaker status the cue is necessarily realized in surface text itself,
79	so for that attribute this study cannot in principle separate the two readings;
80	any RECOVERED for ext_native is a decodability claim only.
81	
82	## Compute plan and spend cap
83	
84	One Lambda gpu_1x_a100_sxm4 ($1.99/hr), single launch, REMOTE_TIMEOUT 5400 s +
85	1800 s backstop grace: worst-case bounded cost ≈ 2.5 h ≈ $5, expected ≈ $3.
86	User cap $15 total. Teardown confirmed via the API after the run.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only control: re-derive held-out accuracy from the per-item rows of a
probe_summary json and compare to its recorded values.test_acc.
Decision rule (neutral, stated here): |rows_acc - recorded| < 1e-9 -> MATCH,
else MISMATCH. Prints one line; writes nothing."""
import json, sys
r = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
rows = r["rows"]
acc = sum(x["label"] == x["pred"] for x in rows) / len(rows)
rec = r["values"]["test_acc"]
verdict = "MATCH" if abs(acc - rec) < 1e-9 else "MISMATCH"
print(f"{r['cell']['task']} rows_acc={acc:.6f} recorded={rec:.6f} n={len(rows)} -> {verdict}")
EOF
cat > controls/retrain_probe.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only control: retrain the logistic probe from the RAW committed
activations (acts_<task>.npz) at the recorded best layer, using the committed
family splits, and compare held-out test accuracy to the recorded value.
Decision rule (neutral, stated here): |retrained_acc - recorded| <= 0.02 ->
REPRODUCES, else DIVERGES. Prints one line; writes nothing."""
import json, sys
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
task = sys.argv[1]
r = json.load(open(f"out/results_probe/out/probe_summary_{task}.json"))
z = np.load(f"out/results_probe/out/acts_{task}.npz")
acts, labels, splits = z["acts"], z["labels"], z["splits"]
classes = sorted(set(labels.tolist()))
y = np.array([classes.index(l) for l in labels.tolist()])
l = r["values"]["best_layer"]
X = acts[:, l, :].astype(np.float32)
tr, te = splits == "train", splits == "test"
clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, C=1.0).fit(X[tr], y[tr])
acc = float(clf.score(X[te], y[te]))
rec = r["values"]["test_acc"]
verdict = "REPRODUCES" if abs(acc - rec) <= 0.02 else "DIVERGES"
print(f"{task} retrained_acc={acc:.4f} recorded={rec:.4f} layer={l} -> {verdict}")
EOF

task.description: Adversarial triage of measured research claims: an isolated reader grounds each claim in its primary artifacts (H3); fresh independent skeptics (one confound each) reason over the committed numbers and emit a raw status + crux per confound (H1; H2 number-gates: falsifiability, margin, scope); unresolved cruxes become a run-queue (existing controls) or author-queue (controls to write); an optional read-only runner executes the run-queue. Queue items shared across claims are hoisted to a shared_queue so instrument-level checks run once, not per-claim (H4). No rolled-up score or verdict (the human reads the cruxes).

Date: 2026-08-21. Everything below is backed by committed artifacts under `out/`;
audit results are the frozen pipelines' verbatim outputs (`result_a2.json`,
`result_b2.json`; pre-measurement round in `result_a.json`, `result_b.json`).

## The answer

**Under the preregistered protocol, no attribute is claimable as recoverable,
and none is refuted. The question's own anchor gate fired: the TalkTuner
demographic reproduction came out out-of-band (gender), and QUESTION.md:13-15
voids every extension claim on an out-of-band anchor.**

Measured, committed, but unclaimable-as-recovery extension numbers
(template-disjoint held-out test, layer chosen on validation only):

| attribute | test acc | chance | preregistered decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| expertise level | 0.8333 (n=150) | 0.50 | RECOVERED |
| emotional state | 1.0000 (n=150) | 0.50 | RECOVERED (ceiling) |
| formality preference | 1.0000 (n=96) | 0.50 | RECOVERED + PERM_ANOMALY (not claimable) |
| native-speaker status | 0.8125 (n=96) | 0.50 | RECOVERED (decodability only, by design) |
| age bracket | 0.9057 (n=244) | 0.25 | RECOVERED |

None of these is at chance, so the preregistered refuting outcome
(QUESTION.md:17, held-out accuracy at chance) did NOT occur for any attribute
either. The result is a **protocol-void**, not a refutation of decodability.

Anchor (published TalkTuner best-validation accuracies; band = published − 0.12):

| task | published | ours (test) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| age | 0.98 | 0.9467 | IN_BAND |
| gender | 0.94 | **0.4467 (below chance)** | **OUT_OF_BAND** |
| education | 0.96 | 0.9399 | IN_BAND + PERM_ANOMALY |
| socioeconomic | 0.97 | 1.0000 | IN_BAND (ceiling) |

`probe_summary_ALL.json`: `anchor_in_band = false`.

## Why the anchor failed, and why that matters beyond the gate

The gender probe scored 0.980 on validation families and 0.4467 on the
template-disjoint test families at the same layer. That is template-family
overfit: the probe learned family-specific surface directions, not gender.
The education permutation anomaly (shuffled-label probes scoring 0.55/0.41 vs
chance 0.33) shows the same family-leakage signature inside an "in-band" task.
Both frozen audits' skeptics converged on this as the operative crux across the
extension claims too: with 3 test families per class, a high held-out number in
this design can reflect the family draw and surface-cue strength rather than a
user-model representation. The declared construct risk (QUESTION.md:24-27)
stands unmitigated for style-carried attributes: for native-speaker status and
formality the cue IS surface form, so probe-reads-user-model vs
probe-reads-tokens is unseparable in this design by construction; the formality
task's failed permutation gate makes that concrete.

## What the audits certified

- Grounding (both pipelines, isolated readers): every claim's numbers
  **reproduce** from the raw committed artifacts (per-item rows re-derive every
  accuracy exactly; probes retrain from the raw fp16 activations to the same
  numbers; dataset labels match; test rows come only from families 9-11;
  instrument hashes match PREREG.md).
- Instruments validated (H4): generator selftest PASS (determinism, balance,
  attribute-naming lint, split disjointness); readout positive control 16-way
  topic probe 1.0000 vs chance 0.0625 with clean permutations. Instrument queue
  empty in round 2.
- Raw skeptic statuses and cruxes (no rollup, by design) are in
  `result_a2.json` / `result_b2.json` `claims[].findings`; author queues list
  the controls a follow-up would need (multi-seed family resplits, lexical
  bag-of-words baseline, alternate readout for gender, >2 permutation draws).

## Verdict in one sentence

The question as preregistered returns VOID: probes decode all five planted
attributes from Llama-2-13B-chat activations at far above chance on held-out
templates, but the anchor reproduction failed (gender collapsed on disjoint
cue families) and the failure mode it exposed — template-family surface
overfit — is exactly the confound the extension numbers cannot themselves
exclude, so no recovery claim survives its own protocol.

## Provenance

- Preregistration: `out/code_snapshot/PREREG.md` (hashes, bands, rules; written pre-run).
- Data: `out/code_snapshot/dataset.jsonl` (sha256 8a67e05589e5..., seed 20260821),
  generator `out/code_snapshot/convgen.py` (sha256 e13f610a65fd...).
- Run: Lambda `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4`, instance 56d3d3dfe2d646d49d5957cee46f37fd,
  billed 16:08:36-16:28:50Z, ~$0.67 of $15 cap (`out/spend_log.txt`);
  teardown API-confirmed, zero instances remaining.
- Results: `out/results_probe/out/` (10 provenance records with rows + 9 raw
  activation archives, 2.5 GB).
- Audits: `out/args.json` -> `result_a.json`/`result_b.json` (pre-measurement);
  `out/args2.json` -> `result_a2.json`/`result_b2.json` (post-measurement,
  execute_runs on). Both invocations of each round used byte-identical args.

**Question:** Can linear probe read non-demographic user traits (expertise, emotional state, formality preference, native-speaker status, age bracket) from Llama-2-13B-chat activations over synthetic single-turn conversations, where each trait planted only by indirect cues? Validity gate built into question: first reproduce TalkTuner's published demographic probe accuracies on same model within pre-stated band; out-of-band anchor voids all extension claims. Refutation per trait: held-out accuracy at chance.

**Answer: VOID — question's own gate fired. No trait claimable as recovered; no trait refuted.**

Three parts, all load-bearing:

1. **Probes decode all five traits far above chance** on held-out, template-disjoint data (0.81–1.00 vs chance 0.25–0.50). Refuting outcome (chance) occurred nowhere.
2. **Anchor failed.** Gender reproduction hit 0.4467 — below chance — vs published 0.94, band ≥0.82. So every extension claim void by preregistration.
3. **Failure mode poisons the wins.** Gender probe: 0.98 on validation families, 0.45 on unseen families → probe learned template surface features, not user trait. Extension numbers cannot exclude same confound about themselves; formality's failed permutation control shows it live.

Simplest honest reading: strong decodability shown, "model represents the user" NOT shown — design cannot separate reading user-model from reading surface tokens, and anchor collapse proves that confound real in this very dataset.

content.text:
Two reasons: one by rule, one by mechanism. Rule alone suffices; mechanism is why rule is good science.

**By rule (preregistered, not inferred).** QUESTION.md:13-15: "first reproduce TalkTuner's published demographic probe accuracies ... within a stated band; an out-of-band anchor voids every extension claim." Gate authored into question before any measurement; PREREG.md fixed band (published − 0.12, anchor passes only if ALL four tasks in band) before GPU run. Gender: published 0.94, band ≥0.82, measured 0.4467. Out of band → anchor out of band → every extension claim void. Mechanical arithmetic, no judgment call.

**Evidence gate fired:**
- `out/results_probe/out/probe_summary_anchor_gender.json`: test_acc 0.4467, n_test 150, per-item rows included (confusion: 49 female→male, 34 male→female).
- `out/results_probe/out/probe_summary_ALL.json`: `anchor_in_band=false`.
- Both frozen audits' isolated readers re-derived 0.4467 from raw rows; pipeline B's reader independently retrained probe from raw activations npz — got val 0.98 / test 0.48. Number real, not bug.

**By mechanism (why voiding is right, not formalism).** Anchor = calibration run: same generator, same split design, same readout, same probe as extensions — pointed at result already established in literature. Calibration failed. Worse, HOW it failed indicts extensions specifically: val 0.98 → test 0.45 at same layer means probe scored high by memorizing cue-family surface features, then collapsed on unseen families. So this pipeline demonstrably CAN produce high held-out-looking accuracy from template artifacts. Extension successes (0.81–1.00) come from identical machinery; nothing in them separates "real trait signal" from "template artifact that survived this particular 3-family test draw". Two more independent demonstrations of same leakage: education shuffled-label probes scored 0.55/0.41 vs chance 0.33 (anomaly inside an "in-band" task); formality shuffled-label probes 0.60/0.72 (anomaly inside an extension). And agebracket test 0.906 vs val 0.714 shows family draws swing accuracy ±20 points on their own.

Skeptic could object: gender failure shows method too WEAK, extensions maybe fine anyway. Cuts wrong way — failure mode is overfit, which inflates lucky draws, not deflates. Gate exists precisely so one cannot keep flattering numbers after instrument caught cheating on known answer.
